title: Research notes
description: Free-text findings from past research batches.

items.name: agentSkill note 1
items.description: The post's '776K combined stars' claim is not supported: humanizer 31.5k and napkin 575 verified on GitHub 2026-09-17; the other 18 links were truncated and are unverified.

items.name: agentSkill note 2
items.description: Skills add procedure; MCP servers add tools. Our stack is tool-heavy and procedure-light.

items.name: agentSkill note 3
items.description: Install safety: read SKILL.md fully, install per-project, pin a commit, never load unvetted skills in a session holding Supabase service keys or API keys, review diffs before updating.

items.name: agentSkill note 4
items.description: Humanizer improves style but does not remove KDP/Etsy duties to disclose AI-generated content.

items.name: agentSkill note 5
items.description: Adoption order: napkin, humanizer -> ffmpeg-skill, video-shotcraft -> graphify, tech-debt-audit -> claude-seo, scroll-world, user-research.

items.name: agentToolkit note 1
items.description: Verified 2026-09-17: obra/superpowers ships via Anthropic's official plugin marketplace; steveyegge/beads is a git-backed issue tracker for agents. The other 38 were not individually verified.

items.name: agentToolkit note 2
items.description: Adopt order: superpowers, beads, serena, repomix, planning-with-files, karpathy-skills, codex-plugin-cc, taste-skill, addyosmani skills, mattpocock skills, claude-hud, rtk.

items.name: agentToolkit note 3
items.description: Risk: headroom/rtk/caveman compress context or output; the accuracy guard rejects numbers missing from source, so never use them on the daily data pipeline or publishing paths.

items.name: agentToolkit note 4
items.description: Risk: terse-output tools strip disclaimers required for finance, health-adjacent and gambling content.

items.name: agentToolkit note 5
items.description: Risk: superpowers, gstack, ECC, oh-my-claudecode and Archon all auto-install hooks; run only one framework at a time.

items.name: agentToolkit note 6
items.description: Install discipline: per-project installs, pinned versions, no unvetted plugins in sessions holding Supabase service keys or API keys.

items.name: agentFramework note 1
items.description: Filter: orchestration stays in n8n, routing in LiteLLM, state in Supabase, building in Claude Code. A framework must do something that stack cannot.

items.name: agentFramework note 2
items.description: dspy is the standout: the golden set + accuracy guard give it a pass/fail metric to optimize local Qwen prompts against.

items.name: agentFramework note 3
items.description: e2b gives generated code a disposable sandbox instead of running beside Sierra Chart or next to keys on the laptop.

items.name: agentFramework note 4
items.description: Speech-to-text is a genuine gap: local Whisper on the RTX 4060 first, Deepgram as the paid fallback; feeds ESP32-S3 recorder audio and consulting call transcripts.

items.name: agentFramework note 5
items.description: agentops adds run traces that model_calls lacks.

items.name: agentFramework note 6
items.description: Risk: crewai, autogen and langchain each want to own orchestration; running one alongside n8n means two drifting descriptions of the same workflow.

items.name: designResource note 1
items.description: Platform mismatch is the whole issue with Webflow/Framer template libraries: they do not produce code that lands in artifacts or Vercel.

items.name: designResource note 2
items.description: Price is not a design property. What reads as expensive: restraint, typography, generous spacing, ONE memorable motion moment, real content instead of placeholder copy.

items.name: designResource note 3
items.description: A template tends to produce a site that looks like that template - which works against premium positioning for a finance-education brand, where the pitch is being different.

items.name: designResource note 4
items.description: The artifact-design skill (already in stack) and taste-skill (on the adopt list) target design judgement more directly than any component purchase.

items.name: designResource note 5
items.description: For client work where the client wants to self-edit afterwards, a Webflow template library becomes genuinely useful - a real scenario for consulting clients only.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #1
items.description: Batch 2 (Oct 9, 2026): 25 sites checked. Already on the list and unchanged: Aceternity UI and Magic UI (adopt). Of the 23 new entries, 12 are adopt, 9 are reference, hold or experimental, and 2 are skip.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #2
items.description: Artifact test: the pages are single self-contained HTML files. Only copy-paste CSS/SVG (Uiverse, CSS Text Effects, MicroKit CSS, Circle Loaders) and one-script-tag libraries (Anime.js) drop straight in. React/Tailwind catalogues (shadcn, 21st.dev, Motion Primitives, mapcn) need a Vercel project with a build step.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #3
items.description: Inspiration galleries (Minimal Gallery, Kage, Refero, AppShot, Component Gallery) show other people's copyrighted designs. Use them to choose a direction and write your own DESIGN.md; never reproduce a real brand or site.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #4
items.description: Licence reality: MIT is stated by Uiverse, CSS Text Effects, MicroKit, shadcn, Anime.js, Motion Primitives, mapcn and Liquid Glass. CC0 is stated by Kitbitz and 3dicons. Kinetics, Circle Loaders, Gradient Buttons, Jiro, Kage, VibePrompt, Refero and Component Gallery state no usable licence: treat as reference until confirmed.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #5
items.description: The biggest find is not a gallery: it is Google's DESIGN.md format (Apache-2.0, alpha). One DESIGN.md per venture, linted for contrast, is the cheapest route to consistent output across pages, Shorts frames and PDFs.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #6
items.description: Prompt libraries (Jiro, VibePrompt, Kage prompts) sell something Claude already does well. The scarce asset is a consistent brand spec, not another prompt.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #7
items.description: Map caveat: mapcn defaults to CARTO basemaps, whose commercial use needs an Enterprise licence per the README; pick another MapLibre-compatible tile source before monetising.

items.name: design-resource note batch2-3 #8
items.description: Batch 3 (Oct 13, 2026), for the upcoming websites: 8 sites checked; 3 were already listed (Minimal Gallery, Refero Styles, 3dicons). Of 5 new: Awwwards, Godly/Recent and Supahero added as free references; Scrolltide on hold ($299, same libraries as the free kit); Mobbin skipped for websites (app-UI library, paid). Workflow for a new site: browse Awwwards (filter GSAP/Three.js) + Supahero + Minimal Gallery, pick ONE direction, write the site's DESIGN.md, build with the free kit.

items.name: gpu vram note #1
items.description: Rule on 8 GB: ONE heavy GPU job at a time. Qwen, Flux, VoiceStudio, Whisper and Stable Fast 3D each want most of the card; the job worker should unload Ollama (keep_alive 0) and restart voice between batches.

items.name: gpu vram note #2
items.description: Use now on 8 GB: Qwen 3.5 9B, VoiceStudio (with restarts), Kokoro, Whisper turbo/small, Flux Q4 GGUF, Stable Fast 3D, Blender + blender-mcp, HyperFrames. Cloud for the rest: TRELLIS.2 on fal, Seedance/Hailuo video.

items.name: gpu vram note #3
items.description: Unlocks at 24 GB, in priority order: (1) Flux FP8 with LoRAs/ControlNet for brand-consistent images, (2) TRELLIS.2 locally (needs Linux), (3) Qwen-Image + AnyAngle multi-angle shots, (4) H3 motion chaining, (5) Whisper large alongside other jobs, (6) bigger local LLM / QLoRA.

items.name: gpu vram note #4
items.description: A 24 GB card does NOT fix licence blockers: Hunyuan3D and HY-World stay excluded for worldwide display; UniMate stays blocked on training-data licences.

items.name: gpu vram note #5
items.description: Open question for the upgrade: where will the 24 GB card live (desktop PC, eGPU, or cloud) and on Windows or Linux? TRELLIS.2 officially supports Linux only.

items.name: gpu vram note #6
items.description: Oct 13 game-studio batch: ACE-Step 1.5 is usable now on 8 GB (music). Catalogued for later: Audio2Face (3D characters), Matrix-Game 5B (concept footage). Beyond reach even at 24 GB: Hunyuan-GameCraft (80 GB recommended).

items.name: VRAM: Qwen 3.5 9B (Ollama)
items.description: Qwen 3.5 9B (Ollama) (Local LLM): needs Fits an 8 GB GPU today at 100% GPU (your own requirement). Exact GB at the quantisation not measured. On 8 GB: Keep as the local ops model; unload it (keep_alive 0) before ComfyUI or voice jobs. At 24 GB: Room for a bigger local model or longer context; pick after measuring quality on the golden set.

extra.source: brain: infrastructure.machines (local machine constraint 'must show 100% GPU')

items.name: VRAM: VoiceStudio / OmniVoice
items.description: VoiceStudio / OmniVoice (Voice): needs About 1 GB at load (third-party estimate, Spheron). Open bug: memory grows with each call (one user saw 5 GB to nearly 20 GB over 3 weeks). On 8 GB: Use it, but restart the voice model between batches or apply the empty_cache +.cpu workaround; never leave it running beside Flux. At 24 GB: Headroom hides the leak but does not fix it: keep the restart rule.

items.name: VRAM: Kokoro TTS
items.description: Kokoro TTS (Voice): needs Small; also runs on CPU (not measured). On 8 GB: Drafts and fallback. At 24 GB: No change.

items.name: VRAM: Supertonic 3
items.description: Supertonic 3 (Voice): needs CPU only (runs on a production server). On 8 GB: Fallback voice on a production server. At 24 GB: No change.

items.name: VRAM: Whisper (speech to text, word timestamps)
items.description: Whisper (speech to text, word timestamps) (Transcription): needs tiny/base ~1 GB, small ~2 GB, medium ~5 GB, turbo ~6 GB, large ~10 GB. On 8 GB: turbo (~6 GB) or small (~2 GB) for caption and voice-over timing; run alone on the card. At 24 GB: large (~10 GB) alongside other jobs.

items.name: VRAM: FLUX.1 dev (ComfyUI images)
items.description: FLUX.1 dev (ComfyUI images) (Images): needs FP16 24 GB, FP8 ~13 GB, GGUF Q4_0 ~7 GB. On 8 GB: GGUF Q4_0 only; slow (about 1m42s per 1024px image listed for a 4060); one LoRA at a time. At 24 GB: FP8 (~13 GB) with LoRAs and a ControlNet (~3.6 GB each); FP16 only just fits.

items.name: VRAM: Stable Fast 3D
items.description: Stable Fast 3D (3D assets): needs ~6 GB. On 8 GB: Free local image-to-3D for quick props and greybox. At 24 GB: Keep as the fast draft step before TRELLIS.2. Beyond VRAM: Stability Community Licence: register, show 'Powered by Stability AI', free under $1M revenue

items.name: VRAM: HyperFrames / HTML-to-video exporters (video rendering)
items.description: HyperFrames / HTML-to-video exporters (video rendering) (Video render): needs No GPU needed (headless Chrome + ffmpeg; ~256 MB RAM per worker). On 8 GB: Use now. At 24 GB: GPU encoding/faster capture possible; not needed.

items.name: VRAM: blender-mcp + Blender
items.description: blender-mcp + Blender (3D clean-up): needs Blender viewport works on 8 GB; heavy Cycles renders slower. On 8 GB: Use now for mesh clean-up and GLB export. At 24 GB: Faster Cycles renders.

items.name: VRAM: TRELLIS.2 (Microsoft)
items.description: TRELLIS.2 (Microsoft) (3D assets): needs At least 24 GB (official); tested on A100/H100. On 8 GB: Use hosted on fal ($0.25-0.35 per model). At 24 GB: Run locally IF the machine runs Linux (official support is Linux only; Windows/WSL untested). Beyond VRAM: Linux only

items.name: VRAM: Qwen-Image-2.1 + AnyAngle LoRA
items.description: Qwen-Image-2.1 + AnyAngle LoRA (Images (multi-angle)): needs ~16 GB. On 8 GB: Skip (GGUF quants exist but quality drops and minutes per image). At 24 GB: Unlock: multi-angle product and character shots locally.

items.name: VRAM: H3 motion-context chaining (ComfyUI)
items.description: H3 motion-context chaining (ComfyUI) (Video): needs Documented floor: a heavily offloaded 12 GB card. On 8 GB: Keep the small-chunk workflow (owner decision). At 24 GB: Revisit: local H3 with motion-context chaining. Beyond VRAM: Open-weight H3 licence excludes US/EU/UK/South Korea; read before publishing

items.name: VRAM: Hunyuan3D-2.1 (open weights)
items.description: Hunyuan3D-2.1 (open weights) (3D assets): needs 10 GB shape, 21 GB texture, 29 GB both. On 8 GB: Skip; use TRELLIS.2 on fal. At 24 GB: Technically fits shape+texture in two passes. Beyond VRAM: Licence excludes EU/UK/South Korea, including displaying outputs there: still skip after the upgrade

items.description: HY-World 2.0 (Tencent) (3D worlds): needs Not published; paper: ~10 minutes per scene on a data-centre H20. On 8 GB: Skip. At 24 GB: Probably still too heavy; re-check if a consumer version ships. Beyond VRAM: Same territory licence as Hunyuan

items.description: UniMate (motion for any skeleton) (3D animation): needs Not stated (diffusion transformer). On 8 GB: Skip. At 24 GB: Re-check VRAM once licensing is cleared. Beyond VRAM: Training-data licences (Mixamo etc.) block commercial use

items.description: Audio2Face-3D (lip-sync) (3D animation): needs Not stated (CPU fallback exists). On 8 GB: Not needed yet (no 3D talking characters). At 24 GB: Re-check when 3D characters arrive.

items.name: How to shrink AI-generated 3D meshes for games
items.description: AI 3D generators output roughly a million evenly sized triangles (they build the shape on a voxel grid and wrap it with marching cubes). Four tools to get to game size: (1) Simplify / edge collapse (QEM; Blender's Decimate > Collapse) keeps the overall shape but deletes fine shallow detail first, such as eyes and lips, and leaves messy slivers with no edge flow; fine for props, statues and rocks. (2) Voxel remesh (Blender Remesh > Voxel) seals holes and fuses overlaps but guesses the surface; thin parts like capes can vanish and small block sizes blow the budget. Use it to clean, then simplify. (3) Retopology (by hand, or QuadriFlow / Instant Meshes, or Tripo and Meshy smart topology) gives clean quad loops needed for anything that bends. (4) Bake a normal map from the high-poly original onto the low-poly model to bring back surface detail; it fakes lighting, not the silhouette. Rough budgets: background props a few hundred to ~2,000 triangles; mobile characters ~5,000-15,000; PC/console hero characters ~50,000-150,000; ship several LODs. Characters: rebuild or repaint the face separately, because simplifying erases it.

extra.source: Nikhil Shahane, 'How to shrink a 3D model from a million triangles to 20,000' (part 3 of a 3D crash course, AssetFurnace project)

items.name: Character-first content: one persona beats 100 one-off images
items.description: Lesson from a Japanese creator-economy article on AI personas: as image models improve, good-looking AI images stop being scarce, so the value moves to a consistent character people follow. Define name, look, voice, personality, daily life, world and posting schedule before generating; keep the look fixed across posts; post as a continuing story so each post leads to the next (polls that shape tomorrow's post work well). Treat the funnel as six steps (post, profile, pinned post, product page, first purchase, repeat), keep most posts non-selling, make paid content clearly deeper than free, and run one character for weeks before judging what works. Be open that the character is AI. Applies to mascots, brand characters and recurring channel hosts.

items.name: Modular character kit: separate face, pose and outfit references
items.description: Pattern from Japanese AI-persona creators who publish free face, pose and outfit reference databases: keep each part of a recurring character as its own reusable reference set, then combine them per post with a multi-reference image editor ('keep this face, use this pose, change into this outfit'). Outfit references are generated text-to-image with no person in them, so they never carry a real product photo; check them against real brands anyway. Make the library browsable: category tabs with counts, search over an English description of each image, a 'copy description' button that becomes the prompt draft, and full-size downloads. Licence pattern: free commercial use of what you make, no redistribution of the raw images, no real people or minors. Applies to any recurring character (channel host, mascot, game hero) and to props: e.g. a fixed set of containers and plates for a recipe channel so clips stay consistent. Multi-reference editing in the library: FLUX.2 klein 4B (local), Nano Banana and Seedream through fal.ai.

items.name: Godot AAA-polish starter kit
items.description: Default add-on set for every Godot 4 game (all MIT, active, verified 2026-10-29): Maaack's Game Template (menus, options, pause, loading), G.U.I.D.E (input, rebinding, controller prompts), Phantom Camera (cinematic cameras), LimboAI (NPC behaviour trees and state machines), Dialogue Manager (text dialogue Claude can write), Godot Shader Warmup (no first-use stutter), Debug Draw 3D (tuning), GdUnit4 (tests), plus Virtual Joystick for mobile/web. 3D outdoor games add Terrain3D, Sky3D, ProtonScatter and gdTree3D; 2D games add Importality or Aseprite Wizard. Turn on built-in engine features before adding plugins: Jolt physics (Godot 4.4+), physics interpolation, SDFGI or VoxelGI, volumetric fog, SSAO/SSIL/SSR, glow, mesh LOD and occlusion culling. Optimise imported AI meshes with meshoptimizer/gltfpack first. Every entry is listed under category godot-addons.
